author: The Infographics Show
description:
When a shipping container falls off a ship, it doesn’t simply disappear beneath the waves. Some sink to the ocean floor, others float for weeks like hidden steel obstacles, and their cargo can travel thousands of miles before washing up on distant beaches.

This video explores what really happens to containers lost at sea, from millions of Lego pieces and Nike shoes drifting across oceans to containers carrying dangerous chemicals like sulfuric acid. We examine why massive cargo ships lose containers during storms, how parametric rolling and overloaded stacks can trigger catastrophic collapses, and why the real number of lost containers may be far higher than official industry figures suggest.
The consequences can last for decades. Steel containers rust on the seafloor, plastics and chemicals spread through marine ecosystems, while partially submerged containers can become nearly invisible hazards capable of tearing into smaller vessels.
